steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Let's add a new feature—bots. Bots can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.

Any chat member can create and manage bots via the user interface:
- open the account settings page (`/account/edit`)
- click the bot icon ("Set up chat bots")

This opens the bots page (`/bots`). It lists the bots you created (administrators see all bots) and has the "Add a chat bot" button. The button opens the `/bots/new` page with a form:

- bot avatar (optional)
- bot name (required), labelled "Name the bot"
- the "Save changes" button

Submitting the form creates a bot and redirects back to `/bots`. Each bot on the list shows its name and its unique bot code in a read-only field labelled "Bot code", in the same list item—the code is used to authenticate bot requests. The bot code is a sensitive credential. The bots page shows all of your bots on one page, without pagination.

From the list, you can also edit a bot (name, avatar): each bot has an "Edit <bot name>" link (for example, "Edit Deploy Bot") to its edit page. The edit page uses the same form and has a "Delete this chat bot" button that asks for confirmation. A deleted bot can no longer post messages.

Like any new user, a new bot joins all open rooms. Bots can be added to other rooms the same way as people.

Here is how a bot can post a message:

```
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

Bots can post from shell scripts and CI jobs. The raw request body becomes the message body. No JSON envelope, no field names.

The endpoint responds with:

- `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`
- `422 Unprocessable Content` — empty body and no attachment
- `404 Not Found` — bad room id
- `401 Unauthorized` — invalid bot code

The message is broadcast to connected clients and triggers push notifications exactly as a human-authored message would.

The message shows the bot (its name) as the author.

  include Avatar, Bannable, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.insert_all(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end

      messages_me_class: "message--me",
      messages_mentioned_class: "message--mentioned",
      messages_threaded_class: "message--threaded",
      messages_page_url_value: room_messages_url(room)
    }, &
  end

  def messages_tag(room, &)
    tag.div id: dom_id(room, :messages), class: "messages", data: {
      controller: "maintain-scroll refresh-room",
      action: [ maintain_scroll_actions, refresh_room_actions ].join(" "),
      messages_target: "messages",
      refresh_room_loaded_at_value: room.updated_at.to_fs(:epoch),
      refresh_room_url_value: room_refresh_url(room)
    }, &
  end

  def message_tag(message, &)
    message_timestamp_milliseconds = message.created_at.to_fs(:epoch)

    tag.div id: dom_id(message),
      class: "message #{"message--emoji" if message.plain_text_body.all_emoji?}",
      data: {
        controller: "reply",
        user_id: message.creator_id,
        message_id: message.id,
        message_timestamp: message_timestamp_milliseconds,
        message_updated_at: message.updated_at.to_fs(:epoch),
        sort_value: message_timestamp_milliseconds,
        messages_target: "message",
        search_results_target: "message",
        refresh_room_target: "message",
        reply_composer_outlet: "#composer"
      }, &
  rescue Exception => e
    Sentry.capture_exception(e, extra: { message: message })
    Rails.logger.error "Exception while rendering message #{message.class.name}##{message.id}, failed with: #{e.class} `#{e.message}`"

    render "messages/unrenderable"
  end

  def message_timestamp(message, **attributes)
    local_datetime_tag message.created_at, **attributes
  end

  def message_presentation(message)
    case message.content_type
    when "attachment"
      message_attachment_presentation(message)
    when "sound"
      message_sound_presentation(message)
    else
      auto_link h(ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(message.body.body)), html: { target: "_blank" }
    end
  rescue Exception => e
    Sentry.capture_exception(e, extra: { message: message })
    Rails.logger.error "Exception while generating message representation for #{message.class.name}##{message.id}, failed with: #{e.class} `#{e.message}`"

    ""
  end

  private
    def messages_actions
      "turbo:before-stream-render@document->messages#beforeStreamRender keydown.up@document->messages#editMyLastMessage"
    end

    def maintain_scroll_actions
      "turbo:before-stream-render@document->maintain-scroll#beforeStreamRender"
    end

    def refresh_room_actions
      "visibilitychange@document->refresh-room#visibilityChanged online@window->refresh-room#online"
    end

    def presence_actions
      "visibilitychange@document->presence#visibilityChanged"
    end

    def message_attachment_presentation(message)
      Messages::AttachmentPresentation.new(message, context: self).render
    end

    def message_sound_presentation(message)
      sound = message.sound

      tag.div class: "sound", data: { controller: "sound", action: "messages:play->sound#play", sound_url_value: asset_path(sound.asset_path) } do
        play_button + (sound.image ? sound_image_tag(sound.image) : sound.text)
      end
    end

    def play_button
      tag.button "🔊", class: "btn btn--plain", data: { action: "sound#play" }
    end

    def sound_image_tag(image)
      image_tag image.asset_path, width: image.width, height: image.height, class: "align--middle"
    end

    def message_author_title(author)
      [ author.name, author.bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
    end
end

  def show
    @user = User.new
  end

  def create
    user = FirstRun.create!(user_params)
    start_new_session_for user

    redirect_to root_url
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def prevent_repeats
      redirect_to root_url if Account.any?
    end

    def user_params
      params.require(:user).permit(:name, :avatar, :email_address, :password)
    end
end

Next, I need to focus on how bot *deletion* works. The prompt is very explicit about a "Delete this chat bot" button.

Here's the critical question: What happens to the bot's messages when it's deleted? Given that `User` has `has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy`, a naive `.destroy` would obliterate all the bot's messages. This is likely not desired. The prompt phrasing "A deleted bot can no longer post messages" is a vital clue.

From what I can tell, `User#deactivate` is being called instead. This is the correct move! Instead of physically deleting the `User` record, `deactivate` does the following:

*   It deletes memberships.
*   It sets `status: :deactivated`.
*   Crucially, the user record *remains*.

This has a few crucial advantages:

*   The bot's messages remain in the chat history.
*   `message.creator` still resolves cleanly (no broken links).
*   `User.active` excludes deactivated users, so the bot won't appear in user lists.

Thus, it is expected that the count of `User.active` decreases after the bot is deactivated.

**Here's the crucial step I'm taking:** *Ensuring* that the bot is truly deactivated, and will no longer post messages. To do this, I will implement at least one of the two conditions:

*   A check to make sure the token is valid, so a request including the old bot code will return `401 Unauthorized`.
*   When a bot is deactivated, make sure `bot_token` becomes `nil`. OR make the authenticate_bot function use `User.active.bot` when authenticating.

Finally, let's think about the `bot_code`.

The prompt tells me this is a sensitive credential used for bot authentication in URLs:

`https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages`

I need to make sure this `bot_code` is:

*   URL-safe (no special characters like `/`, `+`, `=`, `.`).

A random alphanumeric string generated with `SecureRandom.alphanumeric(24)` (or 12) fits this description, and it has high entropy (ensuring uniqueness). cat <<'EOF' > app/models/user/bot.rb
module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true
    has_many :bots, -> { active.bot }, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id

    validates :name, presence: true, if: :bot?

    before_validation :set_bot_defaults, on: :create, if: :bot?
  end

  class_methods do
    def authenticate_bot(bot_key)
      id, bot_token = bot_key.to_s.split("-", 2)
      return nil if id.blank? || bot_token.blank?

      if bot = active.bot.find_by(id: id)
        bot if bot.bot_token.present? && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(bot.bot_token, bot_token)
      end
    end
  end

  def bot_key
    "#{id}-#{bot_token}" if bot? && bot_token.present?
  end

  private
    def set_bot_defaults
      self.password_digest ||= ""
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      SecureRandom.base58(24)
    end
end
EOF

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Bot, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      (bot? ? memberships : memberships.without_direct_rooms).delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address, bot_token: nil
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.insert_all(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end
EOF

class BotsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_bot, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @bots = bots_scope.ordered
  end

  def new
    @bot = Current.user.bots.new(role: :bot)
  end

  def create
    @bot = User.new(bot_params.merge(role: :bot, creator: Current.user))

    if @bot.save
      redirect_to bots_url
    else
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    if @bot.update(bot_params)
      redirect_to bots_url
    else
      render :edit, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @bot.deactivate
    redirect_to bots_url
  end

  private
    def bots_scope
      Current.user.administrator? ? User.active.bot : Current.user.bots
    end

    def set_bot
      @bot = User.active.bot.find_by(id: params[:id])
      head :not_found unless @bot
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@bot)
    end

    def bot_params
      params.require(:bot).permit(:name, :avatar)
    end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/controllers/bots/messages_controller.rb
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :authenticate_bot
  before_action :set_room

  def create
    if @message = create_message
      @message.broadcast_create
      head :created, location: message_path(@message)
    else
      head :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticate_bot
      if @bot = User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_key])
        Current.user = @bot
      else
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.rooms.find_by(id: params[:room_id])
      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def create_message
      if attachment = uploaded_attachment
        @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(attachment: attachment, creator: @bot)
      elsif body.present?
        @room.messages.create!(body: body, creator: @bot)
      end
    end

    def uploaded_attachment
      params[:attachment] if params[:attachment].respond_to?(:tempfile)
    end

    def body
      return if request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"

      @body ||= request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8").scrub
    end
end
EOF

# Chat Bots Architecture

## Data Model
Bots are `User` records with `role: :bot` (`User::Role`), implemented via the `User::Bot` concern:
- `users.bot_token`: unique random token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`) generated on create for bots; `nil` for human users and deactivated bots.
- `users.creator_id`: references the `User` who created the bot, allowing `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` to work uniformly for creators and administrators.
- `bot_key` (`"<id>-<bot_token>"`): the credential displayed in the UI ("Bot code") and used in the messaging API URL. Verified with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Reusing `User` means bots automatically inherit:
  - Open-room auto-join (`after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open`)
  - Closed-room membership management (`Rooms::ClosedsController`)
  - Message authorship (`messages.creator_id`), avatars (`User::Avatar`), broadcasts (`Message::Broadcasts`), and push notifications (`Room::MessagePusher`)
- Bots are excluded from human-only surfaces (login, session transfers, account member list, sidebar DM placeholders) via `User.not_bot`.
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, and removes all memberships while preserving historical messages.

## Routes & Controllers
- `BotsController` (`resources :bots, except: :show`): UI for listing (`/bots`), creating (`/bots/new`), editing (`/bots/:id/edit`), and deleting bots. Linked from `/account/edit` ("Set up chat bots") for all members.
- `Bots::MessagesController` (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`): unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint reading raw request body (or `params[:attachment]`) and returning `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`, `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, or `401 Unauthorized`.
EOF

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot generates a bot token and grants membership to open rooms" do

    assert_equal "#{@bot.id}-#{@bot.bot_token}", @bot.bot_key
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.order(:id).pluck(:id), @bot.rooms.order(:id).pluck(:id)
  end

  test "bot requires a name" do
    bot = User.new(name: "", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert bot.errors[:name].any?
  end

  test "authenticate_bot validates active bots with matching key" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "CI Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-wrongtoken")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("999999-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("invalid")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{users(:david).id}-")
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes memberships and invalidates bot_key while preserving messages" do

    assert_nil bot.bot_token
    assert_nil bot.bot_key
    assert_empty bot.memberships
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(bot_key)
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
  end
end

class Bots::MessagesControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do

          assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Room::PushMessageJob do
            post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key), params: "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅"
          end
        end
      end
    end

    assert_response :created
    message = @room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_equal message_path(message), response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
    assert_equal "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅", message.plain_text_body

    # Verify rendered room shows bot name as author
    sign_in :kevin
    get room_url(@room)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_select "##{dom_id(message)}" do
      assert_select ".message__author", text: /Deploy Bot/
      assert_match /Deploy of v1\.2\.3 finished ✅/, response.body
    end
  end

  test "posting a message triggers web push notifications with bot name" do
    task_count = Push::Subscription.count - users(:kevin).push_subscriptions.count
    # hq has david, jason, jz, kevin (plus @bot who has 0 subscriptions).
    # In fixtures, let's check how many push subscriptions belong to hq members:
    expected_deliveries = Push::Subscription.joins(user: :memberships)
      .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: @room).where.not(user: @bot))
      .merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
      .count

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(expected_deliveries).with do |message:, **|
        payload = JSON.parse(message)
        payload["title"] == @room.name && payload["body"] == "Deploy Bot: Build green"
      end

      post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key), params: "Build green", headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
      assert_response :created
    end

    pool = Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.delivery_pool
    start = Time.now
    while pool.completed_task_count < expected_deliveries
      raise "Timeout waiting for pool tasks" if Time.now - start > 0.5
      sleep 0.01
    end
  end

  test "posting special characters with curl-style form content-type preserves raw body" do
    raw = "Build 100% done & ready=true\nNext line"
    post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: raw,
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }

    assert_response :created
    message = @room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_equal raw, message.plain_text_body
  end

    assert_difference -> { @room.messages.count }, 1 do

    assert_response :created
    message = @room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_equal message_path(message), response.headers["Location"]
    assert message.attachment?
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
  end

      post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key)
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key), params: "   "

    assert_response :unprocessable_content
  end

  end

  test "room the bot is not a member of returns 404 Not Found until added" do

    assert_not_includes closed_room.users, @bot

    end
    assert_response :unauthorized
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
  end
end

class WebPush::Pool
  attr_reader :delivery_pool, :invalidation_pool, :connection, :invalid_subscription_handler

  def initialize(invalid_subscription_handler:)
    @delivery_pool = Concurrent::ThreadPoolExecutor.new(max_threads: 50, queue_size: 10000)
    @invalidation_pool = Concurrent::FixedThreadPool.new(1)
    @connection = Net::HTTP::Persistent.new(name: "web_push", pool_size: 150)
    @invalid_subscription_handler = invalid_subscription_handler
  end

  def queue(payload, subscriptions)
    subscriptions.find_each do |subscription|
      deliver_later(payload, subscription)
    end
  end

  def shutdown
    connection.shutdown
    shutdown_pool(delivery_pool)
    shutdown_pool(invalidation_pool)
  end

  private
    def deliver_later(payload, subscription)
      # Ensure any AR operations happen before we post to the thread pool
      notification = subscription.notification(**payload)
      subscription_id = subscription.id

      delivery_pool.post do
        deliver(notification, subscription_id)
      rescue Exception => e
        Rails.logger.error "Error in WebPush::Pool.deliver: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
      end
    rescue Concurrent::RejectedExecutionError
    end

    def deliver(notification, id)
      notification.deliver(connection: connection)
    rescue WebPush::ExpiredSubscription, OpenSSL::OpenSSLError => ex
      invalidate_subscription_later(id) if invalid_subscription_handler
    end

    def invalidate_subscription_later(id)
      invalidation_pool.post do
        invalid_subscription_handler.call(id)
      rescue Exception => e
        Rails.logger.error "Error in WebPush::Pool.invalid_subscription_handler: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
      end
    end

    def shutdown_pool(pool)
      pool.shutdown
      pool.kill unless pool.wait_for_termination(1)
    end
end

**A Eureka Moment in the Debugging Depths**

Right, let's break this down. That test run just unveiled two critical insights, and frankly, I'm thrilled!

First, in the realm of `WebPush::Notification`, it seems like the `encoded_message` is constructed using `JSON.generate` with `payload["options"]["body"]`, not `payload["body"]`, which explains why the assertions in `test/models/room/push_test.rb` passed! The crucial link in that test lies in `perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do`. By running the jobs within the test's transaction, and with the thread pool, we avoided an earlier `Mocha::ExpectationError`, that the `WebPush::Pool` was trying to catch with its rescue statement. The assertion would have failed if the arguments for the `payload` were incorrect, but because the error was in the thread, it was caught. The key was to ensure the expectations were correct and that the code was run in a way that the assertions would have run, in the thread pool, and that `payload["options"]["body"]` was correct.

But, the real game-changer? That `ActionController::BadRequest` error! The test output illuminated the issue perfectly: `invalid %-encoding`.  It's all about how `curl -d` defaults to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.  When someone sends a request like `curl -d "Build 100% done & ready=true" ...`, Rails' `ActionDispatch::Request#POST` (and consequently, `params`) tries to decode the body as URL-encoded data. But, that percent sign blows it up. This, specifically, crashes when `params[:attachment]` is accessed (or any access to `params` that triggers the POST parser), giving us a 400. And, to top it off, that means ANY `%` sign in the body causes this to happen.

Now, we need to trace this in detail. If a CI script uses `curl`, it might run into this. So, does accessing `params[:room_id]` or `params[:bot_key]` cause the parsing to happen? Digging deeper, Rails merges `path_parameters`, `query_parameters`, and `request_parameters` when `params` is accessed. Good news: `request.path_parameters[:bot_key]` and `request.path_parameters[:room_id]` *don't* touch the POST body. If we check `request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"` before accessing `params[:attachment]`, it skips the form-urlencoded parsing entirely.

But, hang on: What about `authenticate_bot` and `set_room`? These use `request.path_parameters[:bot_key]` and `request.path_parameters[:room_id]`. Wait, but what about params? Calling `params[:bot_key]` calls `request.parameters` which merges POST parameters AND parses form data! So, even `params[:bot_key]` or `params[:room_id]` in a `before_action` *would* cause a crash if the body has a `%` and the `Content-Type` is form-urlencoded. We need to be careful and use `request.path_parameters` instead (or configure `ActionDispatch::Request` to avoid `params` for non-multipart requests). And we need to test how built-in Rails features, such as parameter filtering, might trigger parsing. Let's build a test with `request.path_parameters` and send a malformed form-encoded request. Brilliant!

    end

      @room = @bot.rooms.find_by(id: request.path_parameters[:room_id])

    end

      end
    end

      return unless request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"

      params[:attachment] if params[:attachment].respond_to?(:tempfile)
    end

    def body
      return if request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"

      @body ||= request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8").scrub
    end
end

The core of the problem is this: when someone sends data to my application using `curl -d`, like `"Build 100% finished ✅"` (or any data without explicitly setting the `Content-Type`), `curl` defaults to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.  Rails, because of how `ActionController::Instrumentation` calls `request.filtered_parameters`, which ultimately hits `request.POST`, attempts to URL-decode this data as form parameters. But, special characters like the check mark are not correctly decoded when using `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`! The encoding fails, and the application throws a `400 Bad Request` (`ActionController::BadRequest`) with a "invalid %-encoding" error. If the `action_dispatch.request.request_parameters` environment variable is already set in the request headers *before* the `super` call within a controller's `process_action` method, and the `request.media_type` isn't "multipart/form-data," a few key things happen. First, and this is crucial, Rails completely bypasses the standard Rack form/JSON parsing of the raw request body. It just doesn’t touch it. Second, the `request.raw_post` method *still* retrieves the untouched, raw body bytes as sent by the client. It really is raw! Third, this means that malformed data, like what comes from `curl -d "Build 100% done & ready=true"` or even incomplete JSON like `curl -d '{"invalid json'`, just *works* without throwing an `ActionController::BadRequest` error. It’s pretty robust in this scenario. And finally, if it *is* a "multipart/form-data" request, we *don't* pre-set `"action_dispatch.request.request_parameters"`, so Rails handles the multipart parsing correctly, making `params[:attachment]` accessible as expected.

I also double-checked the execution order. It looks like `Bots::MessagesController#process_action` *does* execute before `ActionController::Instrumentation#process_action`, if the former is defined. The `Bots::MessagesController#process_action` method wraps the `super` method, which then calls `ParamsWrapper#process_action` and *then* `Instrumentation#process_action`.

This is important because `request.raw_post` does its work independently; it reads `rack.input` and caches it in `env["rack.input"]` (and `@raw_post`), and does this completely independent of `action_dispatch.request.request_parameters`.

I think this information has implications for how we're testing this functionality. class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :authenticate_bot
  before_action :set_room

  def process_action(*)
    unless request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
      request.set_header("action_dispatch.request.request_parameters", {})
    end

    super
  end

  def create
    if @message = create_message
      @message.broadcast_create
      head :created, location: message_path(@message)
    else
      head :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticate_bot
      if @bot = User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_key])
        Current.user = @bot
      else
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.rooms.find_by(id: params[:room_id])
      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def create_message
      if attachment = uploaded_attachment
        @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(attachment: attachment, creator: @bot)
      elsif body.present?
        @room.messages.create!(body: body, creator: @bot)
      end
    end

    def uploaded_attachment
      return unless request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"

      params[:attachment] if params[:attachment].respond_to?(:tempfile)
    end

    def body
      return if request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"

      @body ||= request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8").scrub
    end
end
EOF
